Lock request was rejected by the system.
Allows this launcher to turn off the screen and lock the phone. It claims no other device admin policy.
This is the only permission that lets an app lock the screen. Nothing else is requested.
Alternative to Device Admin. This service does not read the screen; it only performs the system lock action when you double tap the home screen.
Pick \"DoubleTap Launcher\" under Installed apps. On a sideloaded build you may first need Settings ▸ Apps ▸ DoubleTap Launcher ▸ ⋮ ▸ Allow restricted settings.
Double tap an empty part of the home screen to lock the phone.
The gesture only exists on this launcher\'s own home screen. That is deliberate — it is what makes the home screen and the app drawer reliably distinguishable.

Device Admin is the smoother route on a sideloaded build. The accessibility service does the same job without Device Admin, but Android 13+ hides its toggle behind \"Allow restricted settings\" first.
To uninstall, revoke Device Admin above first — Android blocks uninstalling an active device admin.
